1.note: The author is using the word translated as **And** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
The word **Shittim** is the name of a place.
The author is speaking of the Moabite women as if they were **daughters** born to the nation of Moab. Alternate translation: [the women of Moab]

2.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the daughters of Moab. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the daughters of Moab called to the people]

The author is using the possessive form to describe **sacrifices** that these people offered to **their gods**. If this is not clear in your language, you could express the meaning explicitly. Alternate translation: [for the sacrifices that they offered to their gods]

Prostrating themselves was a symbolic action by which the Israelites showed worship and submission to their gods. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [bowed down to the ground before their gods to show that they worshiped them]

3.note: Here the author is speaking as if the Israelites were animals that had been **yoked to Baal of Peor**. He means that the people bound themselves to the worship of that god. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [bound itself to the worship of Baal of Peor]

The expression **was yoked** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Israel yoked itself]

The author is using the phrase **the nose of Yahweh burned against Israel** as a common expression of the culture to mean that Yahweh became very angry with the Israelites. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh became very angry with Israel]

4.note: This could mean: (1) that Moses was supposed to seize and execute all the Israelite leaders, even those who had not worshiped Baal. Alternate translation: [every one of the heads of the people] (2) that Moses was supposed to seize and execute only the Israelite leaders who had worshiped Baal. Alternate translation: [all of the heads of the people who worshiped Baal]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the leaders of the people as if they were the **heads** of the people. In this culture, the head was thought of as the leading part of the body. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the leaders of the people]

Here, the word translated **hang** could mean: (1) that the leaders would be executed and their bodies hung up. Alternate translation: [and kill them and hang their bodies] (2) that the leaders would be impaled and their bodies left there. Alternate translation: [and impale them]

This could mean: (1) that the leaders were hung in Yahweh’s presence. Alternate translation: [in Yahweh’s presence] (2) that leaders were hung for the sake of or as a sacrifice to Yahweh. Alternate translation: [for Yahweh’s sake] or [as a sacrifice to Yahweh]

Here, **the sun** represents the open daylight, where everyone could see. Yahweh means that this should be done publicly. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in open daylight where everyone can see]

Yahweh is using **the burning of the nose of Yahweh** as a common expression of the culture to refer to his anger, and for it to **return** means that his anger will stop. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [let the fierce anger of Yahweh turn away]

5.note: Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Let each one of you kill the men under his authority]

Here Moses is speaking as if these people were animals that had been **yoked to Baal of Peor**. He means the people who bound themselves to the worship of that god. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the ones who have joined themselves to the worship of Baal of Peor]

The expression **being yoked** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones who have yoked themselves]

6.note: The author is using the word translated as **behold** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Here the author is introducing **a man from the sons of Israel** as a new participant in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [a certain man who was an Israelite]

Here the author is introducing **the Midianitess**, a woman from Midian, as a new participant in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [a certain woman from Midian]

The author is using **to the eyes of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in the sight of” or “in the presence of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in the presence of Moses … in the presence of all of the congregation]

The pronoun **they** refers to Moses and the rest of the congregation of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Moses and all these Israelites were weeping]

7.note: Here the author is introducing **Phinehas**, a priest, as a new participant in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [a certain priest named Phinehas, who was the son of Eleazar and the grandson of Aaron]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [saw what the man had done]

8.note: The pronoun **her** refers to the Midianite woman whom the man of Israel had brought near. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to the Midianite woman’s stomach]

The expression **was restrained** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [God held back the plague]

9.note: You could translate the number **24,000** according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [twenty-four thousand]

10.note: The author is using the word **saying** to introduce a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

11.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of his anger as if it were **heat** that could be turned back. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [has turned away my anger]

Here, Yahweh could be using the possessive form to refer to: (1) the **jealousy** that he himself feels. Alternate translation: [with the jealousy that I have] (2) **jealousy** for the sake of him, Yahweh. Alternate translation: [with jealousy for me]

Yahweh is repeating words with related meanings, **jealous** and **jealousy**, as a common expression of the culture to emphasize how strongly Phinehas was jealous for Yahweh. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [by him being intensely zealous for my honor]

The words **and I did not finish** introduce the result of Phinehas being jealous with Yahweh’s jealousy. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [and so I did not destroy the sons of Israel in my jealousy]

Yahweh is using **in my jealousy** as a common expression of the culture to refer to his zeal that his people worship him alone. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in my zeal that they worship me alone]

12.note: The word translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [Because he did that, say, ‘Behold me, giving to him my covenant of peace.]

The words that Moses is to speak contain a quotation within a quotation. If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is giving to him his covenant of peace]

Yahweh is using **Behold me, giving** as a common expression of the culture to indicate that he is about to do something, in this case, that he is now giving Phinehas his covenant. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to give to him]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my covenant that he will prosper peacefully]

13.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of Phinehas’s descendants as if they were his **seed**. Just as a plant grows from seed, so descendants come from a person. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and for his offspring who come after him]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **priesthood**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [serving as priests forever]
The word **because** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before.

14.note: The expressions **being struck** and **was struck** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the one whom Phinehas struck, whom he struck]
The words **Zimri** and **Salu** are the names of men.

The author is using **a house of a father** as a common expression of the culture to mean “clan” or “extended family.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [an ancestral clan]

The author is not referring to a specific **Simeonite**. He means the Simeonites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [for the Simeonites]

15.note: The expression **being struck** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Midianite woman whom Phinehas struck]
The word **Kozbi** is the name of a woman, and the word **Zur** is the name of a man.
The pronoun **He** refers to Zur, the father of Kozbi, not to Kozbi herself. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Kozbi’s father Zur]

Here, the word translated as **peoples** could refer to: (1) a division of a people group that is the same size as **a house of a father**. The phrase **a house of a father** explains for readers what **peoples** means. Alternate translation: [was a head of peoples, that is, a head of a house of a father in Midian] (2) a division of a people group that is made up of several individual “houses of a father.” Zur would be the leader of several houses of a father. Alternate translation: [was a head of peoples, over several houses of a father in Midian]

Here the author is speaking of Zur as if he were the **head** of these people. In this culture, the head was thought of as the leading part of the body. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the ruler over peoples]

16.note: The author is using the word **saying** to introduce a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

18.note: The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is the reason for the command that Yahweh gave. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before.

Yahweh is repeating words with related meanings, **deceptions** and **deceived**, as a common expression of the culture to emphasize how thoroughly the Midianites deceived the Israelites. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [by thoroughly deceiving you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **deceptions**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [by their deceitful acts]

Yahweh is using **on the matter of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “concerning” or “in connection with” something. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [concerning Peor and concerning Kozbi … concerning Peor]
The pronoun **their** refers to the Midianites. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the sister of the Midianites]

The expression **being struck** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the one whom Phinehas struck]
